paragraphs.title: The Plunderer's Downfall and the Prayer for Salvation

answers: As one who spoils and deals treacherously
easy.explanation: The enemy is described as one who spoils and acts treacherously.
easy.q: How is the enemy described at the beginning of the passage?

easy.explanation: They pray, “O Lord, be gracious unto us.”
easy.q: To whom does the people appeal for help?

easy.explanation: They ask Him to be their arm and their salvation in trouble.
easy.q: What does the people ask the Lord to be?

medium.explanation: The spoiler will himself be spoiled, and the treacherous will be dealt with treacherously.
medium.q: What principle governs the punishment of the spoiler?

answers: The noise of the tumult and the lifting up of the Lord
medium.explanation: The people flee at the noise, and the nations are scattered when the Lord rises.
medium.q: What causes the nations to flee and be scattered?

medium.explanation: Spoil means property taken from a defeated enemy.
medium.q: What does “your spoil” refer to in these verses?

answers: The enemy acts treacherously, while God's people turn to Him in prayer
The enemy prays, while Israel gathers spoil
The enemy flees, while Israel acts treacherously
challenge.explanation: The enemy is condemned for his actions, while God's people seek mercy and salvation.
challenge.q: What is the chief contrast between the enemy and God's people in this passage?

answers: The enemy's power is broken and its possessions are taken
The enemy becomes stronger and more united
challenge.explanation: The scattered nations and gathered spoil signify the enemy's defeat.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the gathering of the spoil after the nations scatter?

answers: The people pray to the Lord, the nations scatter, and the spoil is gathered
The spoil is gathered, the people pray, and the enemy grows stronger
The nations scatter, Israel acts treacherously, and the enemy prays
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from prayer to divine action and finally to the enemy's downfall.
challenge.q: Which sequence best summarizes the passage?

paragraphs.title: God's Exaltation and the Treasure of Reverence

easy.explanation: The verse says that He dwelleth on high.
easy.q: Where does the Lord dwell according to the passage?

easy.explanation: The Lord has filled Zion with judgment and righteousness.
easy.q: With what does the Lord fill Zion?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “the fear of the Lord is his treasure.”
easy.q: What is called the Lord's treasure?

answers: Wisdom, knowledge, and strength of salvation
medium.explanation: The passage names wisdom, knowledge, and strength of salvation.
medium.q: What things are connected with the stability of the times?

answers: The Lord is lifted up and supreme
The Lord is hidden and weak
medium.explanation: To be exalted means to be raised high and supreme.
medium.q: What does “the Lord is exalted” mean in this context?

answers: They display His righteous rule, while His fear is His treasured possession
They cause Zion to be abandoned
medium.explanation: The Lord fills Zion with judgment and righteousness, and His fear is called His treasure.
medium.q: How are judgment and righteousness related to the fear of the Lord?

answers: Reverence for God provides spiritual stability and understanding
Reverence for God prevents all knowledge
Reverence for God concerns only material wealth
challenge.explanation: The passage joins the fear of the Lord with wisdom, knowledge, and stability.
challenge.q: What may be inferred from the connection between the fear of the Lord and wisdom?

answers: The exalted Lord fills Zion with judgment and righteousness
The Lord's dwelling causes Zion to be emptied
There is no relationship between the Lord and Zion
challenge.explanation: The verses connect the Lord's exalted position with the blessing of Zion.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the Lord's dwelling place and Zion's condition?

answers: The Lord is first described, followed by the blessings and values associated with Him
The enemy is first described, followed by a description of the sea
The spoil is first described, followed by a description of ruin
challenge.explanation: The passage begins with God's exaltation and continues with stability, salvation, wisdom, and righteousness.
challenge.q: What idea structure appears in these two verses?

paragraphs.title: The Desolation of the Land and God's Rising

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “The highways lie waste.”
easy.q: What has happened to the highways?

easy.explanation: The earth mourneth and languisheth, and fertile regions wither.

answers: Now will I rise, be exalted, and lift up myself
Now will I flee and hide myself
Now will I build a ship
easy.explanation: The Lord repeats “now” as He announces His rising and exaltation.
easy.q: What does the Lord declare three times?

answers: Crying, deserted highways, broken agreements, and lost fertility
medium.explanation: The passage describes crying, abandoned roads, broken covenant, and a languishing land.
medium.q: What contributes to the sense of desolation in the land?

answers: Human efforts will produce something worthless and weak
The land will produce a great harvest
The nations will find a safe shelter
medium.explanation: Chaff and stubble are light and useless, symbolizing a fruitless result.
medium.q: What does “Ye shall conceive chaff, ye shall bring forth stubble” mean?

answers: To show that they will be consumed in fire
To show that they will flourish
medium.explanation: Both images emphasize material that is burned and destroyed.
medium.q: Why are the people compared with burnings of lime and cut thorns?

answers: From the land's desolation to God's intervention and the destruction of the wicked
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from national ruin to the Lord's rising and the burning of the enemy.
challenge.q: What is the main movement from the beginning to the end of this section?

answers: The immediate change in the Lord's action
challenge.explanation: The repeated word highlights the moment when the Lord rises and acts.
challenge.q: What does the repetition of “now” emphasize?

answers: The land's ruin precedes the description of the enemy being consumed by fire
The fire causes the land to flourish
The desolation is caused by building highways
challenge.explanation: The section moves from the ruined land to the burning of the hostile people.
challenge.q: How are the desolation and the fire related?

paragraphs.title: Who Can Stand Before the Fire

answers: Those who are far off and those who are near
Only the people of the wilderness
easy.explanation: The Lord addresses both those who are far off and those who are near.
easy.q: To whom does the Lord announce what He has done?

easy.explanation: The sinners are afraid, and fearfulness surprises the hypocrites.
He shakes his hands from holding bribes.
easy.q: What does the upright man do concerning bribes?

answers: Walking righteously, speaking uprightly, rejecting oppression and bribes, and turning from evil
Robbing, betraying, and hiding the truth
medium.explanation: The passage lists upright speech, rejection of oppression and bribes, and refusal to hear or see evil.
medium.q: Which actions characterize the righteous person?

medium.explanation: The hypocrites are contrasted with the person who walks righteously.

answers: A secure dwelling, bread, and sure waters
medium.explanation: He will dwell on high, have a strong defense, and receive bread and dependable water.
medium.q: What is promised to the person who walks righteously?

answers: The sinners fear the devouring fire, while the righteous person finds security
The sinners are protected, while the righteous person is burned
They are described in exactly the same way
challenge.explanation: The sinners fear the fire, but the upright person is promised protection and provision.
challenge.q: What is the contrast between the sinners and the righteous person?

answers: To present righteousness as a complete way of life
To explain how spoil is gathered
challenge.explanation: The righteous person is upright in speech, money matters, treatment of others, and personal choices.
challenge.q: Why does the passage mention both social conduct and avoidance of evil?

challenge.explanation: Bread and reliable water represent the Lord's provision and safety.
challenge.q: What do the bread and sure waters symbolize at the end of the section?

paragraphs.title: From Terror to the Enemy's Disappearance

answers: The king in his beauty and a very far-off land
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty.”
easy.q: What will the eyes see at the beginning of the section?

answers: Concern about the scribe, the receiver, and the one who counted the towers
An abundance of bread and water
easy.explanation: The questions about officials, payments, and defenses express fear and uncertainty.
easy.q: What causes the heart to meditate terror?

answers: The fierce people with difficult speech
The people praying to the Lord
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Thou shalt not see a fierce people.”
easy.q: Which people will no longer be seen?

answers: From terror and concern to the disappearance of the enemy
From joy to fear of peace
From security to a shortage of water
medium.explanation: The people first meditate terror, but eventually the foreign people are no longer seen.
medium.q: How does the people's emotional condition change in this passage?

medium.explanation: The term describes a people perceived as powerful and threatening.
medium.q: What does “a fierce people” mean in this context?

answers: They represent officials, resources, and defenses that seem to be lacking
They show that the enemy disappears immediately
medium.explanation: The repeated questions express anxiety about administration, tribute, and fortifications.
medium.q: Why are the scribe, receiver, and tower-counter mentioned?

answers: The vision of security replaces terror of the enemy
The land is abandoned because of a lack of water
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from fear toward a future in which the threatening people are gone.
challenge.q: What is the connection between seeing the king and land and the disappearance of the foreign people?

answers: The foreign people speak a language difficult for others to understand
The people speak clearly to everyone
The people cannot speak at all
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes speech that is difficult for the hearer to perceive.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the phrase “a people of a deeper speech”?

answers: To express concern about missing officials and defenses
To describe the fertility of the land
challenge.explanation: The questions emphasize the fear that administrators, resources, and defenses have disappeared.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of the repeated questions beginning with “Where is”?

answers: As a quiet habitation and a tabernacle that shall not be taken down
As an abandoned city without water
easy.explanation: Jerusalem is described as quiet, secure, and firmly established.
The verse declares, “the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our king.”
easy.q: Who is Israel's judge, lawgiver, and king?

answers: Forgiveness of iniquity and freedom from sickness
easy.explanation: The inhabitants will be forgiven their iniquity and will not say, “I am sick.”
easy.q: What will the people receive at the end of the passage?

medium.explanation: The rivers form a protective setting through which enemy ships cannot pass.
medium.q: What do the broad rivers and streams symbolize around the city?

answers: It will not be moved or removed
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a dwelling that remains firmly in place.
medium.q: What does the phrase “shall not be taken down” mean about the tabernacle?

answers: Its prey will be divided as abundant spoil
medium.explanation: The enemy's defeat results in the dividing of abundant spoil.
medium.q: What will happen to the enemy according to the passage?

answers: They portray Jerusalem as stable and protected under the Lord's government
They describe a city constantly on the move
challenge.explanation: The fixed tabernacle, protective waters, and divine rule form a picture of security.
challenge.q: How do the tabernacle, rivers, and God's rule work together in the passage?

answers: After the enemy is defeated, the people receive forgiveness and freedom from sickness
The enemy's defeat makes the people ill
There is no relationship between the two matters
challenge.explanation: The passage ends with the people forgiven and free from sickness after the enemy's defeat.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the enemy's defeat and the people's healing?

answers: The Lord holds every governing and saving authority
Leadership is divided among many nations
challenge.explanation: The three titles present the Lord as the complete ruler and savior of His people.
challenge.q: What does the combination “judge,” “lawgiver,” and “king” emphasize?
